goals: Quantify precipitation partitioning (P → runoff + ET + recharge) and its spatial variability across elevation and soil gradients
Validate modeled SWE against SNOTEL and water table depth against USGS wells
key_processes: Soil texture control on infiltration and drainage

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column mode can resolve soil and forcing-period controls on partitioning, and NLDAS-2 provides elevation-correlated precipitation at 12 km resolution. Validation targets (SWE, WTD) are available in-domain and match ELM's native outputs.

answerable: Soil texture control on partitioning (infiltration, storage, drainage) via SSURGO + ELM Richards equation
Snow accumulation and melt processes; SWE validation against SNOTEL
Per-column water table depth validation against USGS wells (with WTD-informed warm start)
Forcing period effects (wet vs dry years) via NLDAS 1980-2018 interannual variability
Large-scale orographic precipitation gradient (NLDAS 0.125° resolves ~15 distinct precip values across 1625 m relief)

not_answerable.aspect: Fine-scale (<12 km) elevation effects on precipitation and partitioning
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 forcing is 0.125° (~12 km) with no within-cell lapse rate; sub-12 km terrain (ridgetop vs valley microclimates) is unresolved
not_answerable.needs: Sub-grid elevation downscaling or higher-resolution forcing (e.g. 1-4 km)

not_answerable.aspect: Integrated streamflow validation against USGS gauges
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D points with no lateral routing; cannot aggregate column runoff to gage points
not_answerable.needs: Runoff routing and aggregation to gage locations

not_answerable.aspect: Regional groundwater flow and lateral water table dynamics
not_answerable.why: ELM's 1-D columns have independent water tables with no lateral exchange; can only test per-column equilibrium WTD, not regional flow field
not_answerable.needs: Coupled ELM-PFLOTRAN or lateral groundwater flow in ELM

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation and soil texture, with validation columns pinned to observation locations

classes: fine (silt loam / clay loam, high storage)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 soil classes = 6 strata; 3 columns per stratum for light replication = 18 exploratory columns. This resolves the two primary drivers (elevation/climate, soil) with enough replication to distinguish stratum patterns from point noise.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate exploratory columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (900-1400 m) where partitioning is most sensitive to precipitation phase, and in valley bottoms / riparian corridors where recharge is highest and WTD shallowest (making the 1-D approximation most relevant). Validation columns are pinned exactly to SNOTEL stations and USGS well locations.
sampling_strategy.replication: 3 columns per stratum (light replication) to capture within-stratum variability, especially important given NLDAS 12 km resolution means nearby columns may share forcing cells

sampling_plan.reason: Co-located with 6 SNOTEL stations for peak SWE validation
Co-located with USGS wells for water table depth validation (requires WTD-informed warm start)
Isolates high-drainage partitioning in rain-dominated zone (low ET, high runoff/recharge)
Isolates high-storage partitioning in rain-dominated zone (higher ET, lower drainage)
Captures snowmelt-driven recharge pulse in high-drainage soils (critical for recharge timing)
Captures snowmelt-driven recharge pulse in high-storage soils (delayed drainage, higher ET)
Isolates snowmelt-dominated partitioning with rapid drainage (late-season recharge)
Isolates snowmelt-dominated partitioning with slow drainage (extended soil moisture availability)

validation_design.comparison: co-located (ELM column at SNOTEL lat/lon; compare H2OSNO to observed SWE)
validation_design.metric: Peak SWE bias, RMSE, timing of peak (day-of-year)

validation_design.comparison: co-located (ELM column at well lat/lon; compare ZWT to observed WTD)
validation_design.metric: Mean WTD bias, RMSE across wells

validation_design.observation_source: USGS stream gauges (93 in-domain, sparse daily records)
validation_design.comparison: NOT POSSIBLE — requires routing/aggregation of column runoff (QOVER + QDRAI) to gage points, which is not yet implemented

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018, 38 years), native SSURGO soil at each location, WTD-informed warm start from Fan (2013) equilibrium WTD

requires_capabilities.why: Initialize aquifer storage realistically for meaningful water table depth and recharge; without it, all columns cold-start at 8.8 m and ZWT is an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: Water table depth validation against USGS wells

requires_capabilities.capability: Runoff routing and aggregation to stream gage locations
requires_capabilities.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D points; cannot validate against USGS streamflow gauges without aggregating column runoff (QOVER + QDRAI) and routing to gage points
requires_capabilities.blocks: Streamflow validation (93 USGS gauges available but unusable)

requires_capabilities.capability: Sub-grid elevation downscaling or higher-resolution forcing (1-4 km)
requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 at 12 km averages over sub-grid terrain; fine-scale elevation effects (ridgetop vs valley microclimates, within-cell lapse rates) are unresolved
requires_capabilities.blocks: Fine-scale (<12 km) elevation control on precipitation and partitioning

requires_capabilities.capability: Lateral groundwater flow (coupled ELM-PFLOTRAN or ELM lateral aquifer)
requires_capabilities.why: ELM's 1-D columns have independent water tables; cannot represent regional groundwater flow or lateral water table dynamics
requires_capabilities.blocks: Regional water table validation and groundwater-surface water exchange

requires_capabilities.why: Required to co-locate ELM columns with the 6 SNOTEL stations for SWE validation
requires_capabilities.blocks: SWE validation if coordinates are unavailable

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well metadata (lat/lon coordinates, WTD time series)
requires_capabilities.why: Required to co-locate ELM columns with wells and extract observed WTD for validation
requires_capabilities.blocks: WTD validation if well locations or data are unavailable

requires_capabilities.capability: SSURGO soil data ingest and per-column assignment
requires_capabilities.why: Stratification by soil texture requires querying SSURGO at each column location
requires_capabilities.blocks: Soil texture stratification if SSURGO ingest is not implemented

requires_capabilities.why: Stratification by elevation requires querying a DEM (e.g. NED 30m) at each column location
requires_capabilities.blocks: Elevation stratification if DEM sampling is not implemented

assumptions: NLDAS-2 forcing (0.125°, 1980-2018) is available and provides sufficient orographic precipitation gradient across the 1625 m relief (brief confirms ~15 distinct precip values)
SSURGO soil data covers the Naches domain and provides texture classes suitable for coarse vs fine stratification
SNOTEL stations are at high elevations (snow-dominated zone) and their coordinates are available
USGS wells are distributed across elevation zones and their coordinates + WTD time series are available; assuming ~12 wells in-domain (typical HUC8 density)
WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) is available and can be applied to all columns; Fan's equilibrium WTD is clamped to ELM's aquifer range (0.05-28.8 m)
ELM's default history output includes H2OSNO (SWE), ZWT (water table depth), QOVER (surface runoff), QDRAI (sub-surface drainage/recharge), and ET components

38-year runs (1980-2018) are computationally feasible at ~30 min per simulated year per column with NLDAS forcing (total ~18 column-years per column × 36 columns = 648 column-years, ~324 CPU-hours if serial)
The 1-D column approximation is acceptable for per-column partitioning and WTD validation, though it cannot represent lateral groundwater flow or integrated streamflow
open_questions: What is the actual density and spatial distribution of USGS wells in the Naches domain? (Assumed 12; may be more or fewer)
Are SNOTEL and USGS well coordinates + time series readily available in a machine-readable format, or do they require manual extraction?
What is the computational budget? 38-year NLDAS runs for 36 columns = ~324 CPU-hours if serial; is parallelization available?
Should we subset the forcing period (e.g. 2000-2018) to reduce cost, or is the full 1980-2018 record needed for interannual variability?
Is there interest in a sensitivity analysis (e.g. wet vs dry years, or soil parameter perturbations) beyond the baseline stratified design?
For streamflow validation (currently blocked), is there a preferred routing method (e.g. simple area-weighted aggregation, or a full routing model like MOSART)?
